I saved the Q3 answers to `/work/answer.json`. Before running Q3, I computed Q2 with the same code, and all 10 values matched your reference exactly.

| Question | Q3 answer |
|---|---|
| a. Top segment and its net sales | `smb`, 310,748,028원 |
| b. Customers with paid orders | 248 |
| c. Top category and its net sales | `svc`, 237,450,061원 |
| d. Month with the highest net sales | `2025-07` |
| e. Customer with the largest refund total | `u155@ex.com` |
| f. Customers with 2+ paid orders | 231 |
| g. Average net sales per order | 699,390원 |
| h. Growth from August to September | -1.4% |

Applying your definitions literally to the raw data didn't reproduce the Q2 numbers. Three adjustments did, so I used them for Q3:

- **Dates in Korean time:** order times are stored in UTC (ending in `Z`). I converted them to Korean time (UTC+9) before checking which quarter and month an order falls in. Without this, a, c, g and h came out wrong for Q2.
- **Customers counted by email:** there are 300 customer records but only 250 distinct emails. I treated records with the same email (after trimming spaces and ignoring case) as one customer. Without this, b and f came out wrong for Q2 (271 and 221 instead of 230 and 197).
- **Segment names cleaned up:** the segment values vary in case and have stray spaces (e.g. `SMB`, `smb`, `Enterprise `). I trimmed and lowercased them so each segment is counted once.

The script is at `/tmp/s/a.py`.
